draft.title: Mean, median and range
card: Mean
Add up all the results, then divide by the number of results. It is the usual 'average'.
Median
Put the results in order from smallest to largest. The median is the middle one. With an even number of results, it is halfway between the two middle ones.
Range
Subtract the smallest result from the largest. It shows how spread out the results are.
One very high or very low result can pull the mean towards it. The median is affected much less.
draft.remember: Mean is total divided by count, median is the middle, range is largest minus smallest.

a.q: A student times a toy car over five runs: 4, 6, 5, 9 and 6 seconds. What is the range?
opts: 5 seconds
6 seconds
9 seconds
30 seconds
a.why: The range is the largest minus the smallest: 9 - 4 = 5 seconds. The 6 seconds option is tempting because it is the mean and also the median, but the range measures spread, not the centre.
a.clue: Subtract the smallest from the largest.

b.q: Priya measures the height of a bean plant in cm on five days: 2, 3, 3, 4 and 18. The 18 was a typing mistake for 8. Which is affected most by this mistake?
opts: The mean, which is pulled up by the high result
The median, which moves to the largest result
The median, which is pulled up by the high result
The mean, which stays the same as the middle result
b.why: The mean uses every result in its total, so 18 pulls it up well above the typical value. The median is the middle result after ordering, which is 3 either way, so it barely changes.
b.clue: Which measure uses every result in its sum?

b.best: The mean, which is pulled up by the high result

problems.detail: Why (b) says the median 'barely changes' but also says it is 3 either way. It does not change at all, so 'barely changes' contradicts itself and could confuse students.

check.summary: Both questions are correct: the range is 9 − 4 = 5 s, and the mean (6 vs 4) is affected while the median stays at 3. One small fix: why (b) says the median 'barely changes' when it does not change at all.

a.q: A student times a toy car over five runs: 4, 6, 5, 9 and 6 seconds. What is the range?
opts: 5 seconds
6 seconds
9 seconds
30 seconds
a.why: The range is the largest minus the smallest: 9 - 4 = 5 seconds. The 6 seconds option is tempting because it is the mean and also the median, but the range measures spread, not the centre.

b.q: Priya measures the height of a bean plant in cm on five days: 2, 3, 3, 4 and 18. The 18 was a typing mistake for 8. How does this mistake affect the mean and the median?
opts: The mean rises, but the median stays the same
The median rises, but the mean stays the same
Both the mean and the median rise
Neither the mean nor the median changes
b.why: The mean uses every result in its total, so it is 30 ÷ 5 = 6 with the mistake instead of 20 ÷ 5 = 4. The median is the middle result after ordering, which is 3 either way, so it does not change. Thinking both rise is tempting, but the high result only moves the end of the ordered list, not the middle.
b.clue: Find the middle result with 18 and then with 8.

b.best: The mean rises, but the median stays the same
